purpose: Sketch of a series of translators, version 2 (decision 5 of .steering/20261028-multilingual-survey): the departure of each translation from the mean of the three at the same place in the story, as relief, so that the common movement of the story is taken out and only what differs between the translators is drawn. Images only.
fixed_before_running: Written on 2026-10-28 and committed before the script was run. A choice made after seeing values: the first sketch (conditions 4bada1f, results 4267d46) was seen, its 180 tiles nearly alike under the common scale, the runs spanning V about -0.02 to 0.25 and A about -0.18 to -0.01, the Spearman correlations by position V 0.75-0.89 and A 0.65-0.72. The researcher chose this version on 2026-10-28 (AskUserQuestion). Not seen before: any departure, its scale, the noise reference, any tile of this version. Changed after the review before running (no high finding): the first-second split added as an upper reference, the place of the runs named in not_claimed, runs with fewer than two matched terms stop, the hash of the base conditions taken from the bytes read, the per-run values recorded.
base_conditions: works/conditions/sketch_translations.json (texts, extraction, runs N = 60, lexicon, generator, relief, figure: all taken from it unchanged)
departure: d_t,k = x_t,k - mean over the three translations of x_.,k, for x = V and A; a run with no matched term, or with fewer than two, stops the run
scaling: c_x = max over t and k of |d_x| (one number for V, one for A); the tile is the rule at (d_V / c_V, d_A / c_A), so the largest departure is 1 and zero departure is the tile of (0, 0)
noise_reference: matched terms of each run split in two ways, odd and even positions, and first and second half; the standard error of the run mean taken as |mean_1 - mean_2| / 2; reported for each split: sqrt(2/3) times the root mean square of the standard errors (the expected root mean square of a departure from the mean of three under sampling noise alone), with the root mean square of the departures. The odd-even split assumes independent words and is small when neighbouring words are alike; the first-second split also takes the slow change of the scene and is large; they are read as a lower and an upper reference.
reported: the scales c_V and c_A, the two noise references, and per run V, A, Z, the departures and the half-split standard errors
not_claimed: That a departure shows a choice of the translator rather than the sampling of words: the noise reference says how large departures of noise alone would be, and if the departures are not clearly larger, the image shows noise. Each panel is scaled with the others by the largest departure, so the image does not show how large the differences are in the lexicon's units. A departure above the noise references is not by itself a choice of words of the translator: a run k may stand at a slightly different place of the story in each translation, as the scenes take different numbers of words, and that difference enters the departure too.
